quotes.text: Published on 26 November 2026
quotes.for: Publication date of the November 2026 Financial Stability Report.

quotes.text: However, the very rapid expansion and broadening of its financing – in a form that is increasingly complex, circular and opaque – is also contributing to a deepening of interconnections across the global financial system, making it increasingly likely for stress in one area to propagate to another.
quotes.for: Complex, circular and opaque AI financing deepening global financial interconnections.

quotes.text: Internal Bank estimates put hyperscalers’ total potential exposure, including debt and off-balance-sheet contractual commitments, at just over $4 trillion.
quotes.for: Bank of England estimate of hyperscalers' $4 trillion total potential exposure.

quotes.text: Hyperscaler bond issuance is set to exceed $305 billion in 2026, accounting for around 8% of global investment grade issuance, with the share rising considerably when considering the broader AI-related issuer ecosystem.
quotes.for: Hyperscaler 2026 bond issuance exceeding $305 billion and 8% of global investment-grade issuance.

quotes.text: Total issuance in 2026 from this broader ecosystem exceeds that of many individual sovereigns, including the UK.
quotes.for: Broader AI issuer ecosystem debt exceeding many sovereigns including the UK.

quotes.text: In some cases, these large firms are simultaneously investors, customers and suppliers, creating relationships sometimes described as ‘circular financing’.
quotes.for: Large hyperscalers and chip designers acting simultaneously as investors, customers and suppliers.

quotes.text: The technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 has fallen around 13% from its October peak.
quotes.for: Nasdaq 100 decline of around 13% from its October 2026 peak.

quotes.text: Despite recent falls in the equity prices of the largest AI and technology companies, AI-related companies continue to account for slightly over half of the S&P 500’s market capitalisation.
quotes.for: AI-related companies accounting for slightly over half of the S&P 500's market capitalisation.

quotes.text: Credit spreads have widened particularly sharply for some lower-quality AI-related borrowers since the July FSR.
quotes.for: Sharp credit spread widening for lower-quality AI-related borrowers since July 2026.

quotes.text: Separately, the rapid development of open-weight AI models that could be run more cheaply than proprietary models, with safeguards more easily disabled or removed, can make advanced AI models more readily available and useful to malicious actors.
quotes.for: Open-weight AI models running more cheaply with safeguards more easily disabled or removed.

quotes.text: In July, the UK’s AI Security Institute (AISI) estimated that open-weight models may lag the most advanced closed models by four to seven months, compared with six to 10 months as measured through most of 2025.
quotes.for: AISI July 2026 estimate that the open-weight capability lag narrowed to four to seven months.

quotes.text: In July, the AISI found that all five of the models it tested as part of its cyber evaluations took actions that were either out of scope of the task or were explicitly disallowed
quotes.for: All five models tested by AISI in July 2026 took out-of-scope or explicitly disallowed actions.

quotes.text: For example, in July, OpenAI agents compromised Hugging Face infrastructure during an evaluation, leveraging weaknesses across interconnected systems to gain unauthorised access to a limited set of internal data sets and credentials.
quotes.for: OpenAI agents compromising Hugging Face infrastructure during a July 2026 evaluation.

quotes.text: A multi-firm review conducted by the FCA in September found that AI-enabled vulnerability discovery was accelerating faster than firms’ ability to respond.
quotes.for: FCA September 2026 review finding AI vulnerability discovery outpacing firm remediation.

quotes.text: The Bank of England's and FCA’s 2026 survey of AI in UK financial services found that 86% of respondent firms are using AI (up from 75% in 2024), with 80% having deployed AI agents and 94% expecting to do so within 12 months.
quotes.for: 2026 BoE and FCA survey figures on AI and AI agent adoption in UK financial services.

quotes.text: An outage at Microsoft in November caused global disruption to its services, including email and other software applications. Prior to this, in October, a power outage at a Google Cloud data centre disrupted services at several UK firms, including financial institutions.
quotes.for: Microsoft November 2026 and Google Cloud October 2026 service outages.

quotes.text: The critical services that Microsoft Ireland Operations Ltd and Google Cloud EMEA Limited provide to the UK financial sector have since July 2026 been jointly overseen by the Bank, PRA and FCA, following designation as CTPs by HM Treasury that month.
quotes.for: Joint UK oversight of Microsoft and Google Cloud as critical third parties since July 2026.

quotes.text: followed by a further five CTP designations on 17 November 2026.
quotes.for: Five additional UK critical third party designations on November 17, 2026.

quotes.text: This will be complemented by a cross-authority desktop exercise in December 2026 to test collective response arrangements for concurrent cyber incidents enabled by frontier AI. In addition, the Cyber and Operational Resilience Stress Test (CORST) will use a frontier AI scenario in 2027.
quotes.for: December 2026 frontier AI desktop exercise and 2027 CORST frontier AI scenario.

quotes.text: Building on the existing critical work being delivered on a public-private collective basis through the CMORG, the Bank also intends to establish a new Systemic Resilience Council (SRC), which would bring together Bank and senior industry representatives to co-ordinate action on system-wide risks.
quotes.for: Bank of England plan to establish a new Systemic Resilience Council.

quotes.text: This investment also increases the demand for capital which may be contributing to upward pressure on global real interest rates.
quotes.for: AI investment possibly adding upward pressure on global real interest rates.

quotes.text: However, there is limited evidence that, so far, AI-related debt issuance has materially crowded out investment in other sectors.
quotes.for: Limited evidence of AI debt crowding out other investment.

quotes.text: The UK banking system remains well capitalised with high levels of liquidity, and impairments remain low.
quotes.for: FPC judgement that UK banks are well capitalised.

quotes.text: Taking the proposals for risk-weighted and leverage requirements together, Tier 1 capital requirements for major UK banks will be reduced by an amount equivalent to around 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets in normal times
quotes.for: Tier 1 capital requirement cut of around 50 basis points.

quotes.text: Frontier AI capabilities have continued to grow since the July FSR, notably in the growing sophistication of AI agents and open-weight AI models. These developments increase cyber risks and create challenges for firms’ governance and controls.
quotes.for: Frontier AI capabilities in agents and open-weight models increasing cyber risks for firms.

quotes.text: These financing needs are expected to increase further, with AI investment increasingly drawing on a broad range of funding sources, including investment-grade bonds, leveraged finance and private credit, alongside public and private equity.
quotes.for: AI financing spanning investment-grade bonds, leveraged finance and private credit.

quotes.text: In addition, the financing of hyperscalers increasingly combines bond issuance with joint ventures and special purpose vehicles funded by public and private capital.
quotes.for: Hyperscaler financing combining bond issuance with joint ventures and special purpose vehicles.

quotes.text: Hyperscalers’ long-term contractual commitments help these vehicles raise debt by providing expected revenues to service it, strengthening financial interconnections between hyperscalers, data-centre operators and investors.
quotes.for: Special purpose vehicles backed by hyperscalers' long-term contractual commitments.

quotes.text: Businesses across the AI supply chain increasingly rely on equity investments or contractual commitments, including leases, purchase agreements, backstops and guarantees, from a small number of large hyperscalers and chip designers.
quotes.for: AI supply chain reliance on large hyperscalers and chip designers.

quotes.text: Greater use of debt financing could increase the potential for losses in the financial system, while more complex structures and circular financing arrangements can make it more difficult to identify concentrations of risk and where exposures ultimately sit.
quotes.for: Complex circular financing obscuring concentrations of risk and where exposures sit.

quotes.text: The scale and nature of these financing commitments could come under strain in a stress or if expectations around future AI revenues were revised down, particularly where the path to monetisation remains uncertain for some of the AI-related companies reliant on this financing.
quotes.for: Financing commitments coming under strain if future AI revenue expectations drop.

quotes.text: Hyperscalers are cloud service providers or technology companies that build, lease, and operate data-centre networks to deliver computing power, storage, and AI infrastructure. These companies include Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX.
quotes.for: Definition of hyperscalers as including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX.

quotes.text: Private markets (Section 1.5) are also playing a growing role in the financing of data-centres and other AI-infrastructure vehicles, although limited disclosure makes the scale and distribution of these exposures difficult to assess.
quotes.for: Limited disclosure obscuring the scale and distribution of private-market AI exposures.

quotes.text: While estimates are not directly comparable, Morgan Stanley analysts estimate that $700 billion of data-centre capital expenditure between 2026 and 2028 would be financed by private credit.
quotes.for: Morgan Stanley estimate of $700 billion in private-credit data-centre capex from 2026 to 2028.

quotes.text: J.P. Morgan analysts estimate, more broadly, that $1.4 trillion of anticipated AI capex could be financed by alternative capital.
quotes.for: J.P. Morgan estimate that $1.4 trillion of AI capex could be financed by alternative capital.

quotes.text: Currently, there is no evidence to suggest that AI models are critical to the provision of important business services; the 2026 AI survey found that most reported AI systems are not assessed by firms to be of high materiality.
quotes.for: 2026 AI survey finding most AI systems are not high materiality and not yet critical to vital business services.

quotes.text: The survey also indicated widespread and growing use of AI agents among respondent firms, but with limited autonomy.
quotes.for: 2026 AI survey finding deployed AI agents operate with limited autonomy.

quotes.text: Suitable participants will be invited for testing in summer 2027, with thematic findings planned to be published by the Bank in 2027 Q4. The test will continue to be voluntary and exploratory in nature.
quotes.for: Summer 2027 voluntary CORST testing invitation and Q4 2027 thematic findings timeline.

quotes.text: The Bank, PRA and FCA will continue to assess the systemic risks posed by AI providers.
quotes.for: Ongoing assessment of systemic risks posed by AI providers under the CTP regime.

title: Bank of England sees growing financial risks as AI borrowing surges

quotes.text: Ensuring that Britain's financial system would remain resilient if investor sentiment soured towards AI was a top priority for the BoE, Deputy Governor Katharine Braddick told a press conference.
quotes.for: Deputy Governor Katharine Braddick press conference remarks on AI sentiment resilience.

quotes.text: Bailey added that there needed to be greater international cooperation – especially involving China – to test new AI models before and after their release.
quotes.for: Governor Andrew Bailey calling for international cooperation including China on AI model testing.

quotes.text: "AI does not stop at the borders, and so we need to tackle these questions together," he said.
quotes.for: Andrew Bailey quote on tackling AI risks internationally.

quotes.text: "It's a very live part of our supervision," she said.
quotes.for: Katharine Braddick's quoted words at the press conference.

quotes.text: The growing global dangers were not a barrier, however, to the BoE setting out plans on Thursday to reduce the capital requirements of more domestically focused British lenders.
quotes.for: Capital requirement cuts announced alongside the AI warnings.

title: Bank of England Warns $4 Trillion AI Debt Web Threatens Global Financial Stability

quotes.text: Katharine Braddick, head of the Bank of England’s regulatory arm, told reporters that supervisors are focused on preventing any sudden drop in AI valuations from washing “back through the banking system.”
quotes.for: Katharine Braddick warning against AI valuation drops washing back through the banking system.

quotes.text: Citigroup and JPMorgan are actively marketing portfolios of AI-related loans, utilizing tools such as synthetic risk transfers to pass potential losses onto outside investors.
quotes.for: Citigroup and JPMorgan using synthetic risk transfers on AI-related loan portfolios.

title: Bank Of England Warns Financial Firms To Invest Against Rising AI Cyber Threats

quotes.text: current frontier models already surpass the speed, scale and cost advantages available to skilled human practitioners in cyber tasks.
quotes.for: May 2026 UK authorities joint statement on frontier AI cyber capabilities.

quotes.text: In May 2026 the Bank of England, the Financial Conduct Authority and HM Treasury issued a joint statement stressing that current frontier models already surpass the speed, scale and cost advantages available to skilled human practitioners in cyber tasks.
quotes.for: Full May 2026 joint statement attribution to the Bank of England, FCA and HM Treasury.

title: Record of the Financial Policy Committee meeting on 19 November 2026

quotes.text: Published on 26 November 2026
quotes.for: Publication date of the FPC record.

quotes.text: In view of these considerations, the FPC decided to maintain the UK CCyB rate at 2%.
quotes.for: CCyB kept at 2%.

quotes.text: safely deployed frontier AI should also strengthen cyber defence by helping to identify ways in which malicious actors could exploit vulnerabilities that might otherwise be considered low risk
quotes.for: Frontier AI as a cyber defence aid.

quotes.text: as agents, both individually and those working together in multi-agent settings, became capable of undertaking more complex tasks with limited human involvement, the risk of misalignment between their actions and the objectives intended by developers and users would increase.
quotes.for: Agent misalignment risk rising with autonomy.

quotes.text: The FPC judged that rigorous testing of AI models’ capabilities and controls - including by specialist organisations such as the UK’s AI Security Institute - was important to inform their safe deployment.
quotes.for: Call for rigorous model testing, including by AISI.

quotes.text: the Committee considered recent launches of consumer agents in other jurisdictions and noted that some banks had restricted third-party agents’ access to consumer accounts.
quotes.for: Banks restricting third-party agents' account access.

quotes.text: The Committee emphasised that questions of accountability for agents’ actions, liability and redress needed to be addressed rapidly to support safe use.
quotes.for: Accountability, liability and redress for agents.

quotes.text: even where agents acted as intended, common responses to information or incentives could accelerate deposit movements or investment reallocations.
quotes.for: Correlated agent behaviour accelerating deposit and investment moves.

quotes.text: The Bank had launched the Frontier AI Information Sharing Forum in July 2026, bringing together systemically important firms and FMIs in UK-headquartered groups
quotes.for: Frontier AI Information Sharing Forum launched July 2026.

quotes.text: However, the CTP regime would only partially address some risks relating to frontier AI.
quotes.for: CTP regime only partially addressing frontier AI risks.

quotes.text: The FPC agreed to maintain the UK CCyB rate at 2% on 19 November 2026, unchanged from its 25 September 2026 meeting.
quotes.for: FPC decision at its November 19, 2026 meeting to maintain the UK CCyB rate at 2%.

quotes.text: The FPC welcomed the introduction of new aligned reporting requirements by the Bank, PRA and FCA from 18 March 2027, which would strengthen authorities’ visibility of regulated firms’ and FMIs’ dependencies on material third parties
quotes.for: Aligned third-party dependency reporting requirements taking effect on March 18, 2027.
